# action.docker_volume_prune

<!-- Code generated by tools/genskill from the provider schema. DO NOT EDIT. -->

Kind: action. Back to [SKILL.md](../SKILL.md).

Removes volumes no container uses (anonymous ones only, unless `all = true`), like `docker volume prune`, and reports what it removed and the space reclaimed. It acts on every matching object on the daemon, not only on objects Terraform manages, so narrow it with `filters`. The `result` object is the `POST /volumes/prune` response; `volumes_deleted` lists the removed objects.

Actions need Terraform >= 1.14. They keep no state: they run when a
resource's `lifecycle { action_trigger { ... } }` fires, or on demand with
`terraform apply -invoke=action.docker_volume_prune.<name>`. Arguments go inside
the action's `config` block.

## Usage

```terraform
action "docker_volume_prune" "<name>" {
  config {
    # arguments below
  }
}

# Run it: lifecycle { action_trigger { events = [after_create] actions = [action.docker_volume_prune.<name>] } }
# on a resource, or: terraform apply -invoke=action.docker_volume_prune.<name>
```

## Arguments and attributes

| Name | Type | Status | Forces replacement | Sensitive | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `all` | `bool` | optional |  |  | Remove every unused volume, named ones included (`docker volume prune --all`). Default `false`: only anonymous volumes. Needs Engine API >= 1.42. |
| `filters` | `map(string)` | optional |  |  | Prune filters, one value per key: `label` (`key` or `key=value`) and `label!` (the negation). |
| `result_path` | `string` | optional |  |  | Local file the action writes its result object to after a successful run. The file holds one JSON object keyed by the action's output names (`result`, the identity values, the raw outputs with their `*_sha256` hashes, and the version values), with keys sorted at every level, two-space indentation and a trailing newline; it is written atomically (temporary file, then rename) and parent directories are created. Read it in a later run with `jsondecode(file(...))` or the `local_file` data source. Sensitive values are written in full, since this is your own file, but show as `(sensitive)` in the progress message. Nothing is written when the action fails. |

## Example

```terraform
resource "docker_volume" "data" {
  name = "data"

  lifecycle {
    action_trigger {
      events  = [after_create, after_update]
      actions = [action.docker_volume_prune.scratch]
    }
  }
}

# Removes every unused volume labelled scratch, named ones included. On demand:
#   terraform apply -invoke=action.docker_volume_prune.scratch
action "docker_volume_prune" "scratch" {
  config {
    all         = true
    filters     = { label = "scratch" }
    result_path = "${path.module}/.prune/volumes.json"
  }
}
```
